newsitem.title: INDIA: Rapid growth is solution to India's problems--RBI.
newsitem.headline: Rapid growth is solution to India's problems--RBI.

text.p: A high sustained rate of economic growth is the only answer to India's social and economic problems, central bank chief Chakravarty Rangarajan said on Friday.

Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor Rangaqrajan said the rate of growth of the economy had fallen short of expectations, despite achieveing several notable landmarks during the 50 years since independence.
Rangarajan was speaking at a function held in Bombay to celebrate the 50th anniversary of India's independence.

He said foodgrain output had increased to 198 million tonnes in 1996-97 from 50 million in 1950-51, and 1991 census data showed the literacy rate had gone up to 52 percent from 18.3 percent in 1951. Life expectancy had almost doubled to 61 years, he added.

"While the rate of growth of the Indian economy in the last 151008fifty years is significantly higher than what the Indian economy had experienced before independence, it has certainly fallen short of our expectations," Rangarajan said.
And it was lower than that achieved by many other East Asian countries.
"Even the benefits of such a modest rate of growth of the economy have been diluted by a rapid increase in population," the RBI governor said.
Rangarajan expressed optimism about the economy, saying the country had come a long way from the crisis years of 1990 and 1991.
"The foreign currency assets of the RBI today exceed $26 billion," he said. "Our foreign currency reserves, including gold amount to $30 billion."
He added: "The saving rate has shown a rise and the external sector is very much under control."
Rangarajan said that economic policy was aimed at increasing efficiency and there was no reason why India should not achieve and sustain a much higher growth rate in the years to come.
"Ultimately, it is high and sustained growth that will be the answer to India's myriad social and economic problems," he said.
But Rangarajan warned, "The future is neither given nor ordained. We have the skills and if we have the will, we can make it happen."
